articles.title: Quick start: set up Velstrian Tenderworks for your first tender
articles.summary: Configure your organisation profile, upload core corporate evidence, and initiate your first tender workspace.
articles.html:
Who this is for

This quick-start guide is for bid managers, commercial directors, and procurement specialists getting started with Velstrian Tenderworks. Follow these sequential steps to ensure your organisation facts, evidence citations, and AI drafting profiles are configured for real procurement work.

The five steps at a glance

  1. Organisation profile: legal details and accreditations.
  2. Evidence Vault setup: policies, ISO certificates and case studies.
  3. Tender workspace: upload the ITT and the specifications.
  4. Drafting and scoring: answers with citations, scored against PPN 026.
  5. Export the submission: Word, PDF and the compliance matrix.

Step 1: Configure your organisation profile

  1. Navigate to Settings > Organisation.
  2. Confirm your registered legal name, Companies House number, trading name, and primary domain.
  3. Specify your operational sectors (e.g. Facilities Management, Construction, IT Services) and UK regional coverage.
  4. Click Save profile. Velstrian Bid embeds these facts into answer contexts to avoid hallucinated company parameters.

Step 2: Seed the Evidence Vault

Upload foundational corporate proof documents evaluators look for in standard selection questionnaires (SQ) and qualitative envelopes:

  • Certifications: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus.
  • Insurance: Employer Liability (£10m), Public Liability (£5m), Professional Indemnity.
  • Mandatory Policies: Modern Slavery Statement, Health & Safety, Equality & Diversity, Whistleblowing.
  • Carbon Reduction Plan (PPN 006): Baseline emissions and annual reduction targets.
Do not upload outdated or unapproved drafts. Evaluators verify expiry dates and policy signatories during standstill checks.

Step 3: Choose your workspace

  • Velstrian Bid: Supplier-side tender workspaces for parsing ITTs, extracting compliance matrices, mapping TOMs social value, and drafting cited responses.
  • Velstrian Buy: Buyer-side workspace for evaluating submitted supplier packs, applying scoring rubrics, and running moderation sessions.
  • Settings: Central administration for team seats, RBAC roles, audit logs, and Stripe billing.

articles.title: End-to-end bid management workflow in Velstrian Bid
articles.summary: Step-by-step master workflow from procurement document ingestion to compliant submission export.
articles.html:
The Velstrian Bid lifecycle

Velstrian Bid accelerates bid production while enforcing strict evidentiary rigor. The end-to-end workflow comprises five structured phases.

Phase breakdown

Phase Primary activities Deliverables & gates
1. Ingestion Upload ITT, specifications, pricing schedules, and question templates. Extracted requirement checklist & word count constraints.
2. Compliance Matrix Break questions into granular sub-criteria and assign owners. 100% covered compliance matrix with assigned responsibilities.
3. Social Value Mapping Select TOMs measures against contract value (≥10% target). Calculated financial proxy value & delivery method statement.
4. AI Drafting & Citation Generate targeted answers grounded strictly in Evidence Vault proof. Draft responses with verifiable source citations and evidence audit trail.
5. Review & Export Peer review, executive sign-off gate, export to Word / PDF / Excel. Submission-ready response pack with audit archive.

Best practices for bid teams

  • Isolate individual requirements: Do not group multi-part buyer questions into a single paragraph. Break them down so every sub-question has an explicit answer.
  • Verify source citations: Review the evidence side-drawer before approving any drafted response.
  • Track clarification logs: When the buyer issues clarification bulletins, update the affected matrix rows immediately.

articles.title: Procurement Act 2023: compliance & transparency notices guide
articles.summary: Understand the key changes under the Procurement Act 2023 and how Velstrian Tenderworks supports compliance for buyers and suppliers.
articles.html:
Overview of the Procurement Act 2023

The Procurement Act 2023 establishes a consolidated public procurement regime across the UK. It replaces former regulations (PCR 2015, UCR 2016) with a focus on value for money, public benefit, transparency, and integrity.

Key statutory changes

Area Previous regime (PCR 2015) Procurement Act 2023
Award Principle Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), with greater emphasis on social value & environmental benefit.
Transparency Contract Award Notices Mandatory central digital platform notices across planning, pipeline, tender, award, and contract performance.
KPI Publication Internal management only Mandatory public reporting on top 3 contract KPIs for contracts exceeding £5m.
Debrief Letters Unstandardised summary letters Assessment Summaries provided to all tenderers before standstill period begins.

How Velstrian Tenderworks ensures readiness

  1. Transparent Audit Trails: Every scoring decision, evaluation note, and narrative revision is logged with immutable timestamps.
  2. Evidence Traceability: Supplier claims must be linked to verifiable source documents, satisfying the increased transparency requirements.
  3. Standardised Assessment Summaries: Public sector evaluators can generate compliant assessment breakdowns directly from the moderation matrix.

articles.title: Create and structure a Velstrian Bid tender workspace
articles.summary: Enter tender parameters, configure evaluation weighting, and establish a clean procurement project workspace.
articles.html:
Why workspaces matter

A Velstrian Bid tender workspace isolates all documents, requirements, team roles, AI credits, and audit histories for a single procurement competition. Creating dedicated workspaces prevents cross-contamination of client confidentiality and evidence citations.

Step 1: Enter opportunity details

  1. Click Velstrian Bid > New contract.
  2. Contract title: Enter the exact tender title from Find a Tender / Contracts Finder.
  3. Contracting authority: Enter the purchasing body (e.g. Crown Commercial Service, NHS Trust, Borough Council).
  4. Contract value: Enter the estimated total contract value in GBP. This figure is critical for social value threshold calculations.
  5. Submission deadline: Set the exact date and time. Deadlines are automatically tracked in your compliance calendar.

Step 2: Set evaluation weightings

Configure the published evaluation split between commercial and quality criteria:

  • Quality / Technical weighting: Typically 50% to 70%.
  • Commercial / Price weighting: Typically 20% to 40%.
  • Social Value weighting: Enter the weighting this contract notice gives social value. PPN 026 states a minimum of 10% for contracts valued at 1m GBP and above but less than 5m GBP, and 20% at 5m GBP or above, for central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies on procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027. Velstrian Bid warns when the weighting you enter is under that figure and never blocks the entry. Other contracting authorities are not bound by it and may weight social value at whatever figure their notice states.

Step 3: Initialise workspace

Click Create workspace to enter the document upload and compliance extraction interface.

articles.title: Upload, parse and organise procurement documents
articles.summary: Prepare ITTs, specifications, pricing schedules, and appendices for high-accuracy requirement extraction.
articles.html:
Supported document formats

Velstrian Bid natively ingests standard procurement formats including .docx, .xlsx, .pdf, and .csv. Clean native digital files yield the highest extraction accuracy.

Recommended file hierarchy

  • Tender Workspace (one folder per tender)
    • 01_ITT_Instructions_to_Tenderers.pdf
    • 02_Specification_Schedule_2.docx
    • 03_Quality_Response_Template.docx
    • 04_Pricing_Schedule_Appendix_B.xlsx
    • 05_Social_Value_Question_Schedule.docx
    • 06_Clarification_Log_Bulletin_1.pdf

Extraction validation checklist

Once Velstrian Bid processes uploaded documents, review the extracted items:

  • Confirm all scored quality questions are captured with their specific word/character limits.
  • Check that pass/fail mandatory qualification criteria are tagged appropriately.
  • Verify that scoring scales (e.g. 0-5, 0-100) are mapped correctly.
For scanned PDF files, use the OCR validation mode to verify that tables, footnotes, and header numbers were parsed without character corruption.

articles.title: Build an audit-proof compliance matrix before drafting
articles.summary: Turn complex buyer specifications into a matrix of every mandatory obligation, its owner and its evidence.
articles.html:
The importance of a compliance matrix

Non-compliant or partially answered questions are the leading cause of bid disqualifications in UK public procurement. A compliance matrix provides a single pane of glass ensuring 100% coverage of buyer requirements.

Recommended matrix schema

Field Description Example
Ref ID Unique requirement reference matching the tender schedule. SQ-04.2 / Q3_Quality
Buyer Requirement Exact verbatim wording from the specification. "Demonstrate how you will achieve Net Zero Scope 1 & 2 by 2030."
Response Type Evaluation classification. Scored Quality / Mandatory Pass-Fail / Information Only
Owner Assigned bid author or subject matter expert. Lead Bid Writer / Head of Sustainability
Linked Evidence Verified documents cited from the Evidence Vault. ISO-14001-Cert-2026.pdf
Status Current lifecycle state. Not Started > Drafting > Peer Review > Approved

Completion criteria

A requirement row must not be marked Approved until all three conditions are satisfied:

  1. The narrative directly answers every sub-question and complies with word/character counts.
  2. All factual claims cite active documents in the Evidence Vault.
  3. The designated peer reviewer has completed a rubric evaluation.

articles.title: Generate, cite and edit winning bid narratives
articles.summary: Draft with AI grounded strictly in your corporate evidence, edit for evaluative tone, and keep the proof behind every claim.
articles.html:
The grounded drafting engine

Velstrian Bid generates draft responses by synthesizing buyer evaluation criteria with verified corporate facts from your Evidence Vault. Every factual claim is backed by inline citations.

Generation process

  1. Open the target requirement in the Drafting Studio.
  2. Verify the selected context documents in the evidence panel.
  3. Select your organisation's Tone Profile (e.g. Technical Formal, Commercial Crisp, Public Sector Partnership).
  4. Click Generate draft.

Evaluating and refining the draft

Apply the CAR Framework (Context, Action, Result) during editorial review:

  • Context: Acknowledge the contracting authority's specific operational challenges and local priorities.
  • Action: Explain the exact operational methodology, tooling, and governance you will deploy.
  • Result: Quantify the positive outcome, citing historical contract metrics and verified case studies.
Never leave ungrounded assertions (e.g. "We are the leading provider..."). Replace broad assertions with quantified proof (e.g. "Over the past 24 months, our team delivered 99.8% SLA compliance across 14 local authority contracts...").

articles.title: Collaborative review, team assignments & sign-off gates
articles.summary: Manage multi-author bid workflows, review gates (Red, Amber, Gold team reviews), and executive sign-off.
articles.html:
Review gate methodology

Enterprise bids require structured review gates to catch compliance gaps, raise writing quality, and secure executive sign-off prior to submission.

Review stages

Review stage Timing Primary objective
Pink Team (Strategy Review) 20% of timeline Review win themes, compliance matrix completeness, and evidence assignments.
Red Team (Evaluator Simulation) 60% of timeline Score the complete draft against the buyer's published scoring rubric (0 to 5 scale).
Gold Team (Executive Sign-off) 90% of timeline Final commercial sign-off, legal compliance review, and submission authorization.

Setting assignments and permissions

Assign specific section owners and reviewers from the Team & Assignments panel. Reviewers can leave inline commentary, request re-drafts, and approve final responses.

articles.title: Exporting submission packs (Word, PDF, Excel Matrix, Audit ZIP)
articles.summary: Generate clean, client-ready tender submissions in Microsoft Word, PDF, Excel compliance matrices, or complete audit archives.
articles.html:
Export options

Velstrian Bid allows you to export your tender work at any stage into standard buyer-ready file formats.

Available export formats

  • Microsoft Word (.docx): Formatted narrative document including table of contents, question headers, word count counters, and embedded evidence tables.
  • PDF Document (.pdf): Locked presentation copy ready for executive sign-off or direct upload to buyer procurement portals.
  • Compliance Matrix (.xlsx / .csv): Full spreadsheet of all requirements, evaluation criteria, response owners, completion status, and evidence citations.
  • Audit Trail Archive (.zip): Complete cryptographic archive containing all response versions, timestamped revision logs, and referenced evidence attachments.

Export procedure

  1. Open your contract in Velstrian Bid.
  2. Verify that all mandatory requirements are marked Approved.
  3. Click Export in the top action bar.
  4. Select your target format and choose whether to append evidence appendices.
  5. Click Generate Export to download the package.

articles.title: How social value scoring & TOMs proxy calculations work
articles.summary: Understand how committed measures are priced with Oxford Social Value Bank proxy values, and the minimum weightings PPN 026 states.
articles.html:
How TOMs scoring works

TOMs (Themes, Outcomes and Measures) is how UK public sector buyers structure social value commitments so they can be evaluated and quantified in financial terms. Velstrian Bid prices each committed measure with the Oxford Social Value Bank proxy values held in the measure library, so the same commitment produces the same figure every time.

Calculation formula

Total Social Value (£) = ∑ (Measure Proxy Value × Committed Quantity × Duration Factor)

Example measures

The proxy value per unit is held against each measure in the library and shown beside it when you enter a quantity. These are four of the measures Velstrian Bid offers.

Measure code Measure description Unit
JOB_LT_UNEMPLOYED Long-term unemployed person into employment Per person per year
APPRENTICESHIP_12M Apprenticeship created (12+ months) Per apprenticeship
LOCAL_SUPPLY_CHAIN Local SME supply-chain spend Per £100 local spend
VOLUNTEER_HOUR_SKILLED Skilled volunteer hour Per hour

What the summary shows on a PPN 026 contract

Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026. The summary reports your committed proxy value and its share of the declared contract value, with no pass or fail colour, because PPN 026 states a minimum social value weighting in the evaluation and sets no target for committed proxy value.

PPN 026 states a minimum weighting of 10% for contracts valued at 1m GBP and above but less than 5m GBP, and 20% at 5m GBP or above, for the central government bodies it addresses on procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027. It states no minimum below 1m GBP. You record the weighting and the award criteria the notice names in the contract wizard.

articles.title: PPN 06/20 social value themes & Model Award Criteria (superseded)
articles.summary: The five social value themes and Model Award Criteria introduced by PPN 06/20. PPN 06/20 was superseded for procurements commencing on or after 24 February 2025, so this article is a reference for contracts recorded under it.
articles.html:
PPN 06/20 has been superseded. It ceased to apply to procurements commencing on or after 24 February 2025. This article is a reference for contracts recorded under it. Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026, and a contract already recorded under PPN 06/20 stays readable and exportable and keeps naming PPN 06/20.

The Social Value Model as PPN 06/20 defined it

Procurement Policy Note 06/20 asked central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies to evaluate social value with a minimum 10 percent weighting in tender awards. It structured the model into five national priority themes. A PPN is a Cabinet Office instruction addressed to those bodies rather than law, so PPN 06/20 never bound local authorities, NHS bodies or universities.

The 5 national social value themes under PPN 06/20

Theme Focus area Typical buyer objectives
Theme 1: Fighting climate change Environmental sustainability & net zero Carbon Reduction Plans (now PPN 006), waste minimisation, circular economy commitments and biodiversity protection.
Theme 2: Tackling economic inequality Supply chain resilience & skills SME and VCSE supply chain spend, local employment, apprenticeships, digital skills training and prompt payment codes.
Theme 3: Covid-19 recovery / resilient communities Community resilience Physical and mental health support, local community projects, workplace safety and remote collaboration support.
Theme 4: Equal opportunity Fair work & inclusion Reducing disability employment gap, pay equality, inclusive hiring, modern slavery risk management and fair living wage commitments.
Theme 5: Wellbeing Health & community wellbeing Staff wellbeing charters, mental health first aiders, community integration and public health partnerships.

Model Award Criteria (MACs)

A PPN 06/20 tender named one or more Model Award Criteria, for example MAC 1.1 or MAC 2.2, under the theme it belonged to. Velstrian Bid does not map questions to MAC numbers. A contract recorded under PPN 06/20 keeps the theme codes T1 to T5 it was built with.

What Velstrian Bid uses for new contracts

PPN 026, published 5 August 2026, applies to central government procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027 and valued at 1m GBP or more including VAT. Its model has two outcomes, Good jobs and Skills, across six award criteria. It states a minimum social value weighting of 10% from 1m GBP and 20% from 5m GBP.

Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026. In the contract wizard you select the award criteria the contract notice names. Velstrian Bid does not rank the six criteria or choose them for you, because PPN 026 publishes no ordering.

Structuring a high-scoring response

  1. Method Statement: Explain how you will deliver the commitment during contract performance.
  2. Quantitative Metrics: Provide exact numbers (e.g. 5 apprenticeships, £50k local supply chain spend, 25% carbon reduction).
  3. Monitoring & Governance: Name the role responsible for reporting progress to the contract manager.
  4. Evidence Base: Cite historical delivery data or accredited policies from your Evidence Vault.
Vague intentions score low. Evaluators look for commitments that are contractual, measurable and tied directly to the contract delivery location.

articles.title: Oxford Social Value Bank proxy methodology
articles.summary: Detailed guide to the economic assumptions, proxy valuations and measure selection behind the figures Velstrian Bid calculates.
articles.html:
The economic foundation of proxy values

Velstrian Bid prices social value with the Oxford Social Value Bank proxy values, which put a monetary figure on a social or economic outcome using cost-benefit analysis and wellbeing valuation. Every figure the product reports is that proxy value multiplied by the quantity you commit, so it is computed rather than estimated.

Key principles of measurement

  • Additionality: Only benefits created directly as a consequence of the contract are counted. Business-as-usual activities must be excluded.
  • Deadweight: Outcomes that would have occurred anyway are discounted from the proxy valuation.
  • Attribution: Social value must be attributed strictly to the supplier's proportional contribution.

Choosing the right measures

Review the buyer's specification to identify whether they prioritise local economic regeneration or environmental decarbonisation, and tailor your commitments to their stated local strategic plan.

Map each commitment to the taxonomy the buyer's own notice names, and quote that notice's wording rather than a bare theme number. The measure library, the PPN 026 award criteria and the legacy PPN 06/20 themes order their priorities differently, so a number carried across from one framework misreads under another.

articles.title: Carbon Reduction Plans (PPN 006) & Net Zero commitments
articles.summary: How to draft, verify and cite PPN 006 compliant Carbon Reduction Plans for major UK public contracts. PPN 006 replaced PPN 06/21.
articles.html:
The requirement (PPN 006)

PPN 006, Taking account of Carbon Reduction Plans in the procurement of major government contracts, requires bidders for contracts with an estimated value above £5 million per year including VAT to publish a compliant Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP) detailing Scope 1, Scope 2, and a defined subset of Scope 3 emissions. It is addressed to central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies, and applies to relevant procurements advertised on or after 24 February 2025. It replaced PPN 06/21, which carried the same duty under the old numbering.

The NHS requirement is broader. Under the NHS net zero supplier roadmap a Carbon Reduction Plan is required for all new NHS procurements, with no value threshold at all since April 2024.

Mandatory CRP components

Section Required data
Baseline Emissions Historical 12-month baseline footprint (tCO2e) across Scope 1, 2, and 5 mandatory Scope 3 categories.
Current Reporting Year Emissions recorded in the most recent completed financial year.
Reduction Targets 5-year reduction trajectory towards Net Zero (no later than 2050).
Carbon Reduction Projects Completed environmental initiatives and planned future measures (e.g. EV fleet transition, renewable tariffs).
Board Sign-Off Formal director signature within 12 months of tender submission date.

Evidence Vault integration

Upload your signed CRP into the Evidence Vault. Velstrian Bid verifies the publication date and extracts key emissions metrics for automatic inclusion in sustainability narratives.

articles.title: Evidence Vault: managing policies, accreditations & case studies
articles.summary: Build and maintain a single source of truth for corporate certifications, policies, and past contract performance.
articles.html:
The corporate proof library

The Evidence Vault is your organisation's centralized repository of verified proof documents. Velstrian Bid queries the Vault during AI drafting to ensure all answers cite real, current corporate data.

Core evidence categories

  • Accreditations & Standards: ISO certificates, CHAS, Constructionline, Cyber Essentials.
  • Statutory Policies: Health & Safety, Environmental, Modern Slavery, Safeguarding, Anti-Bribery.
  • Insurance & Financials: Policy schedules, audited financial statements, Dun & Bradstreet ratings.
  • Case Studies: 3-page structured past performance summaries with client contacts, values, and quantifiable KPIs.

Maintaining validity & expiries

Every certificate uploaded should have an accurate expiration date. The Evidence Vault alerts administrators 60 days prior to certificate expiration to prevent invalid submissions.

articles.title: Verifiable proof & automated citation mapping in answers
articles.summary: How Velstrian Bid links draft claims to specific Evidence Vault source files, maintaining full audit traceability.
articles.html:
Inline citation mechanism

When Velstrian Bid drafts an answer, it inserts citation references linking each factual assertion directly to an excerpt in an Evidence Vault document.

Citation panel features

  • Source Inspector: Clicking a citation opens the source document side-by-side with the highlighted passage.
  • Evidence Confidence: Displays a match score indicating how closely the draft reflects the underlying evidence document.
  • Export Citation Ledger: When exporting to Word or PDF, an evidence appendix is generated listing all cited documents and section references.

articles.title: Buyer-side supplier management & compliance review
articles.summary: Track suppliers, submitted documents, mandatory qualifications, and evaluation notes from the purchasing authority perspective.
articles.html:
Buyer-side workflow overview

The Velstrian Buy workspace enables procurement officers and evaluation panel members to organize supplier bids, verify qualifications, and manage consensus evaluations in compliance with procurement regulations.

Managing supplier submissions

  1. Navigate to Velstrian Buy > Suppliers.
  2. Select a supplier record to view uploaded SQ responses, insurance certificates, and technical envelopes.
  3. Review pass/fail mandatory criteria (e.g. economic standing, grounds for exclusion).
  4. Record evaluation findings and request clarifications directly through the audit log.

articles.title: Objective evaluation rubrics, moderation & consensus audits
articles.summary: Configure evaluation rubrics, score tender bids objectively, record moderation notes and export consensus audits.
articles.html:
Evaluation workflows

The Velstrian Buy workspace enables procurement teams to evaluate supplier bids transparently in compliance with the Procurement Act 2023.

Standard scoring scale

Score Classification Evaluation standard
5 Outstanding Exceeds requirements with exceptional added value and complete, verified evidence.
4 Good Fully satisfies the requirement with credible evidence and minor areas for improvement.
3 Satisfactory Meets standard requirements, with minor omissions in supporting evidence.
2 Partial Partially addresses the question with significant gaps or unsubstantiated claims.
1 Poor Fails to address core criteria or provides inadequate evidence.
0 Non-compliant No response provided or completely unacceptable proposal.

Consensus and moderation

After individual evaluators record independent scores and commentary, the panel conducts a moderation session. Moderated scores and consensus justifications are recorded with full version control.

Audit log exports

Export the completed consensus matrix and individual scoring records to support debrief letters, standstill notices and audit compliance.

articles.title: Set up your Velstrian Buy workspace and buyer profile
articles.summary: Tell us what kind of organisation is buying, where you buy and in what currency, so the right rules reach every requirement.
articles.html:
Who this is for

Anyone setting up Velstrian Buy for a public body or a private company. The answers here decide which procurement rules apply to every requirement you build.

1. Record what kind of organisation you are

Your organisation type is the fact every later step reads. A council, an NHS body, a school or a university is a public buyer. A company is a private buyer. Set it when you set up your organisation, or later in Settings, Organisation, General. Only an owner or an admin can record it, because it is a fact about the organisation.

Until it is recorded, the requirement builder shows Not recorded yet under Who is buying. Nothing is enforced and nothing is hidden until you answer, and any threshold shown is marked as assumed.

2. Record where you buy

In the same settings page, Jurisdiction records which nation's procurement rules your organisation buys under. It decides which statutory route and duties apply to an award. Leave it unanswered and the product says so rather than assuming one.

3. Set your market and default currency

Market is the country you trade from. Default currency is the currency a new private requirement starts in. Both are preselections you can change on each value. Stored values are never converted.

4. Add your local priorities (public buyers)

In Settings, Products, Velstrian Buy settings, add the outcomes your organisation cares about, each with a social value theme, an area or locality and a weight hint. You attach them to requirements later. The same page shows your tenancy tier, data region and isolation for reference.

What changes between public and private

  • A public buyer sees the Procurement Act 2023 threshold check, the sourcing routes and the social value steps.
  • A private buyer records the document being issued (an RFI, RFP, RFQ or invitation to tender) and an estimated value in its own currency, and social value measures are optional.

articles.title: Build a requirement, from a document or from blank
articles.summary: Start a requirement pack from a draft specification, last year's pack or a business case, or fill it in yourself.
articles.html:
Start a requirement

Go to Requirements and choose New requirement. The builder asks How do you want to start?

  • Start from a document. Upload a draft specification, last year's tender pack or a business case. We read what the document states and suggest a value for each field.
  • Start blank. Fill in every field yourself.

Checking what was read

Each suggestion shows the file and page it was read from. You accept, edit or reject each one, and every decision is recorded with your name. Names, references and dates can be accepted together. Figures, criteria and lots are checked one at a time. Anything not found is listed under Not found in this document for you to fill in. Nothing read from a document is a score.

A figure stated in another currency is not put into a pounds field and is never converted. A scanned document with no text cannot be read, so upload a text copy or type the details.

The first step: contract type and value

  • Give the requirement a name and choose the contract type and value band.
  • Public buyers answer What are you buying? (goods or services, or works) and the estimated total value including VAT, and see which side of the Procurement Act 2023 threshold it falls.
  • Choose the sourcing route you are running. You can change it until bids are submitted.
  • On the non statutory route, record the document you are issuing and, for a private purchase, the estimated value with its currency and tax basis.

articles.title: Local priorities and social value measures (public buyers)
articles.summary: Attach the outcomes your organisation cares about, then choose the social value measures the contract should deliver.
articles.html:
Local priorities

The second step lists the local priorities recorded in your Velstrian Buy settings. Select the ones this contract should advance. With none recorded you can continue and add them later.

Social value measures

The third step offers measures from the social value measure library. When you open it, AI suggests measures for this contract. The suggestion is advisory: check each measure fits before you keep it, or run the suggestion again, or pick measures yourself if AI is unavailable.

The rail shows an estimated social value for the measures you chose. It is calculated from quantities fixed by the contract's value band, so set the value band first.

When measures are required

For a public buyer at least one measure must be chosen before you can continue. For a private buyer measures are optional, because no procurement rule asks a private company for them.

articles.title: Set the award weightings and scoring bands
articles.summary: Enter price, quality and social value weightings from your tender notice, and see the minimum that applies to your organisation.
articles.html:
Award criteria weightings

Enter the weightings from your own tender notice: price, quality and social value. They must total 100 percent before you can continue. These are published with the pack and are the weightings applied when bids are ranked.

Quality

Quality is scored by your evaluation panel as one consensus score on each bid. It is applied only when every bid in the tender has one. Until then it is shown as suspended and weighted at zero, and the evaluation says why.

The social value minimum

The builder tells you which minimum applies to your organisation, if any:

  • Required. A minimum your organisation must meet, with the instrument that sets it.
  • Guidance. You may publish below it, and you record why. The reason is stored on the published pack.
  • None. No UK procurement rule sets a weighting for your organisation.
  • Not recorded. We do not yet know what kind of organisation you are, so nothing is enforced.

Where it applies, the builder also says your organisation must obtain a Carbon Reduction Plan from suppliers.

Scoring bands

Each band carries a descriptor so every evaluator reads a mark the same way. The bands are locked with the weightings at publication.

articles.title: Publish, download and share the requirement pack
articles.summary: Preview the pack, lock the weightings at publication, then download it as PDF or Word to send to suppliers.
articles.html:
Preview and publish

The last step previews the pack: contract type, value band, weightings, local priorities, the measures with their estimated values, and the submission instructions. Publish requirement pack saves it and takes the weight lock.

The requirement narrative

Below the preview you can draft a requirement narrative with AI or write your own. A draft is not part of the published pack until you approve it, and suppliers never see a draft. The figures are checked again when you publish, and the approval is recorded against your name.

Market sounding

The same step offers a market sounding from the published award record: enter a CPV code to see who won comparable contracts, how many bids those tenders drew and the published values. It is free and uses no AI.

What the weight lock does

At publication the price, quality and social value weightings, the award criteria and the scoring bands are hashed and timestamped, before any bid is received. Every evaluation against the pack checks them against that lock and reports any change.

Sharing the pack with suppliers

Publishing records the pack. It does not email suppliers. Open the requirement and use Download PDF or Word (.docx), then send the pack through your usual channel, such as your tendering portal or email.

After publishing

  • A change to an approved narrative is issued as a clarification or an addendum, with a reason every bidder reads in the pack.
  • Withdraw to draft or Archive changes how the pack reads on the register. Neither changes the locked weightings, the digest or the timestamp.

articles.title: Record suppliers in your directory
articles.summary: Add the suppliers you buy from, check them on Companies House, and see their contracts and delivery track record.
articles.html:
Add a supplier

Go to Suppliers and use Add a supplier. Enter the supplier name and, for a UK company, the Companies House number. Check on Companies House confirms the number before you save. A number already in your directory is refused, so open the existing supplier instead.

Why the directory matters

An evaluation adds bids from this directory, so record each bidder here before you score. Awarded contracts are linked to the supplier, and the directory shows each supplier's contracts and delivery track record.

The supplier record

Open a supplier to see its record and the tabs used to manage the relationship after award: commitments, scorecards, concerns, risk, reviews and benefits. The guide on managing the contract covers each one.

articles.title: Open and run an evaluation, with the AI pre-read and consistency check
articles.summary: Score each bid against the published pack. The AI helps you read and checks consistency, and never sets or changes a score.
articles.html:
Open an evaluation

Go to Evaluations, pick a published requirement and, if it has one, a tender reference, then choose Open evaluation. Add a supplier bid for each supplier in your directory that responded.

Score each bid

  • Score each social value measure from 0 to 100.
  • Enter the tendered price, which is the price axis of the award ranking.
  • Enter the panel's consensus quality score from 0 to 100. It is never generated by AI and never derived from the social value score.

A bid missing a figure on a weighted criterion is held out of the ranking rather than scored zero, because a missing figure is an unread bid, not a poor one.

The AI pre-read

For each response you can generate a pre-read. It locates evidence in the supplier's response against each published criterion and quotes it word for word, lists what is not obviously addressed, and never scores, ranks or recommends a mark. A quote is only shown when it can be found in the response. If the pre-read is unavailable, read the response yourself and score as normal. Nothing is blocked.

The AI consistency check

Run consistency check comments on how consistently the panel has scored and what evidence it relied on. It is advisory and never changes a score. When AI is unavailable, or its draft is rejected, a rule based check runs instead and says so.

Limits to keep in mind

  • The panel evaluates and scores every response. The AI is a reading aid.
  • The weightings are checked against the lock taken at publication, and any change is reported above the ranking.
  • Move the evaluation on with Send to moderation and Mark complete.

articles.title: Compare bids, whole life cost and bid normalisation
articles.summary: Lay options side by side, cost each way of delivering a requirement over its whole life, and put supplier prices on one footing.
articles.html:
Comparisons

A comparison holds the options you are weighing up as columns, your criteria as rows, and the judgement a named person made in each cell. New comparison takes three steps: the segment (a CPV code, or none), what goes in (bids received against an evaluation, registered suppliers, options added by hand or market options), and the criteria you weight.

Whole life cost models

In Whole life costs, a model holds each way you could deliver a requirement and what each would cost across the term. You state the term, the price base year and the discounting: the HM Treasury Green Book rate, a rate your organisation states, or none. Nothing is filled in for you, because a figure resting on an assumption you did not make is not your figure.

Bid normalisation

From Whole life costs, Normalise supplier prices turns each supplier's price schedule into one whole life figure over the same term and quantities. Price lines can be one off, per year or per unit. Present value with Green Book rates is optional. Bids in different currencies are shown in separate groups and are never compared or converted.

articles.title: Award a contract: standstill for public buyers, letters for every bidder
articles.summary: Award from the ranking, see the standstill that applies to a public buyer, and draft award and regret letters.
articles.html:
Before you award

Award is available only when every bid on the evaluation is complete. If bids are level on score, social value and price, the evaluation says so. Resolve the tie before you award.

Award and create the contract

Award & create contract on the winning row creates the contract at once, with the social value commitments from the winning bid attached, and takes you to Contracts. Check the ranking before you select it.

Standstill (public buyers)

For a contracting authority, the contracts list shows when the mandatory standstill under the Procurement Act 2023 ends, counted in working days from the award date, with a note on how bank holidays were treated. Do not enter the contract before that date.

A private buyer owes no standstill, and the contracts list says so.

Award and regret letters

The evaluation can draft an award letter for the winner and a regret letter for each other bidder. Drafts are advisory and are not legal advice. Your organisation reviews and approves each letter before sending it. If AI drafting is unavailable, or a draft states a figure, date or period that was not supplied, a standard template letter is shown instead.

articles.title: Manage the contract, commitments and supplier reviews
articles.summary: Record contracts, confirm what the supplier promised, score delivery and run review meetings.
articles.html:
Contracts

An awarded evaluation creates its contract. To add one awarded elsewhere, use Record a contract on Contracts, or Start from the signed contract: we read the title, value and dates it states and you decide what goes into the form.

The supplier's tabs

Open the supplier from Suppliers to manage the relationship:

  • Commitments. Every promise from the supplier's winning bids. Confirm each one to add it to the ledger the supplier is measured against. KPIs and commitments can also be read from the signed contract, as proposals for you to confirm.
  • Scorecards. Score the supplier for each period and choose which scorecards are released to them.
  • Concerns. Concerns raised, the corrective action plans put in place, and commendations.
  • Risk. What the platform has worked out from its own records, and what your team has flagged, kept apart.
  • Reviews. Monthly and quarterly review sessions, with their packs, sealed minutes and signatures.
  • Benefits. Savings and other value claimed against the supplier, and what finance has signed off.

articles.title: Quick RFQ for private sector buyers
articles.summary: Describe a job or upload what you have, check the scope, then download an RFQ pack and a price schedule for suppliers.
articles.html:
When to use it

Quick RFQ is the short route for a private sector purchase with a settled scope, when you want prices back quickly without building a full requirement pack.

1. Start

Choose Describe the job and say what you need, where, by when and how much of it, or Upload what you have (PDF, DOCX or TXT). Your organisation's default currency is chosen for you and amounts are never converted. Set the response and questions deadlines.

2. Review

AI drafts the scope only. It never writes a price, a rate or a term. Each scope item shows where it came from, and you accept, change or remove it. A suggestion whose words could not be found in your brief or document is left out and counted. The price schedule lines carry a description, quantity and unit, with no rate column, because suppliers price them.

Write the timetable and submission instructions yourself, and attach one of your organisation's saved terms templates or choose no terms. Velstrian Tenderworks never writes or suggests terms. Templates are kept in Settings, Organisation, Terms templates.

3. Export

Decide every AI suggestion and choose the terms, then download the RFQ pack (Word or PDF) and the price schedule (Excel). Only accepted and edited items are exported.

articles.title: Bid to a private sector buyer
articles.summary: Start a bid for a commercial buyer, and see what the workspace keeps and leaves off when no procurement statute applies.
articles.html:
Choose who you are bidding to

Choose Start a bid. The first question is Who are you bidding to? Choose Private sector for a commercial buyer running its own process through an RFI, RFP, RFQ or invitation to tender. No procurement statute applies. You can change the answer before the bid is created.

How the bid starts

Drop the RFP, RFQ or invitation pack, the specification and the pricing schedule, or enter the details yourself. Two starting points are not offered for a private bid: Discover lists tenders published by public buyers, and a framework call off is a public procurement route.

What a private bid records

  • The buyer's country, preselected from your organisation's market.
  • The time zone the deadline is stated in. A deadline is never saved without its zone.
  • The value with its own currency. Values are never converted.
  • Every country or region the contract covers.

What the workspace keeps

The documents, requirements, answers, review and submission screens. It leaves off the tools that only UK public procurement law requires: social value, statutory KPIs and the selection questionnaire.

articles.title: Set your market and default currency
articles.summary: Tell Velstrian Bid which country you trade from and which currency new values start in, without changing any public sector rule.
articles.html:
Market

Market is the country your organisation trades from. It sets the tax and identifier labels and the defaults for private bids, such as the buyer's country. It never changes which procurement rules apply to a public bid. With no market saved, one is suggested from your address country, and nothing is stored until you save.

Default currency

Default currency is the currency a new value starts in, for example a private bid, a private requirement, a quick quote or a Quick RFQ. It is a preselection you can change on each value. Velstrian Bid never converts a stored value, and this is not the currency you are billed in.

Where to set them

Both are asked when you set up your organisation, and can be changed at any time in Settings, Organisation, General by an owner or an admin. A Companies House lookup on the same page fills the name, number and address for a UK company.

articles.title: Price a quote for a private buyer with Quick Quote
articles.summary: Turn a buyer's request into a priced quotation, one line at a time, in the buyer's currency.
articles.html:
Start

Open Quick quote. Paste or describe the buyer's request, or upload the buyer's RFQ (PDF, DOCX or XLSX). A Quick RFQ price schedule is read without AI. Name the buyer, choose the currency and check the valid until date, which is 30 days from today unless you change it.

Velstrian Bid keeps every quote on a bid, so you also give the sector, where the work is delivered, the expected value and the duration. These answers are yours and are never filled in for you.

Review and price

AI restates the scope only. It never writes a price, a rate or a term. Accept, change or remove each scope item, then enter a unit rate on each line, typed or taken from your rate card. Totals are shown per currency, with the VAT rate you enter. Amounts in different currencies are never added together or converted.

Cover note, terms and export

A cover note can be drafted from the scope you accepted. It never holds a number and is yours to edit. Attach one of your saved supplier quote terms or choose no terms, then download the quotation.

articles.title: Run a private sector purchase in Velstrian Buy
articles.summary: What changes for a private company buying: the document you issue, your own currency, optional social value and no statutory standstill.
articles.html:
How the product knows you are a private buyer

From your recorded organisation type. A company is a private buyer, and the requirement builder shows it under Who is buying. Until the type is recorded nothing is enforced and nothing is hidden.

Building a requirement

  • Choose the non statutory route and record the document you are issuing: a request for information, a request for proposal, a request for quotation or an invitation to tender.
  • Enter the estimated value in the currency you are buying in, preselected from your default currency. It is stored with its currency and never converted.
  • Social value measures are optional, because no procurement rule asks a private company for them.
  • No UK procurement rule sets a social value weighting for you. Set whatever your own policy requires.

Awarding

No standstill applies to a private buyer, so you are free to enter the contract when you are ready. Award and regret letters are still drafted for you to review.

The short route

For a settled scope, Quick RFQ produces an RFQ pack and a price schedule without a full requirement pack. See the Quick RFQ guide.

articles.title: Enterprise Single Sign-On (SAML 2.0) & SCIM directory sync
articles.summary: Configure identity provider integration (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace) and automated SCIM user provisioning.
articles.html:
Enterprise Identity Integration

Velstrian Tenderworks supports SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM 2.0 automated user provisioning for enterprise accounts, enabling centralized access governance.

SAML 2.0 configuration steps

  1. Navigate to Settings > Security > SSO.
  2. Copy your organisation's ACS URL (Assertion Consumer Service) and Entity ID (Audience URI).
  3. In your Identity Provider (Entra ID, Okta), create a new SAML Application and paste the endpoints.
  4. Upload your IdP metadata XML or paste the IdP SSO URL and X.509 Certificate into Velstrian Tenderworks.
  5. Enable Enforce SSO to disallow password authentication for verified email domains.

SCIM 2.0 user lifecycle management

SCIM synchronization automatically creates users when assigned in your IdP and deactivates access immediately upon employee offboarding, maintaining compliance with security baselines.

articles.title: Enterprise plans, subscriptions, seats & AI credit allocation
articles.summary: Manage subscription tiers, additional user seats, monthly AI generation allowances, and Stripe invoicing.
articles.html:
Velstrian Tenderworks subscription tiers

Velstrian Tenderworks pricing is tiered to accommodate solo bid consultants up to enterprise public sector bidding teams.

Velstrian Bid tiers

Tier Monthly price Seats AI credits
Starter £49 1 200 per month
Pro £149 5 750 per month
Portfolio Contact sales Unlimited 3000 per month

AI credits explained

One AI credit corresponds to one full generation of an answer narrative. Compliance matrix parsing, TOMs scoring calculations, document viewing, and standard exports do not consume AI credits.

Subscription management

Account owners can upgrade plans or add seats anytime via Settings > Billing with instant activation.

The page opens on your plan and its one main action, for example Upgrade to Pro on Starter. A move up starts today and you pay the difference for the rest of the period. A move down takes effect at the end of the period you have paid for.

One control on that page opens the Stripe billing portal: Invoices and card details, in the Payment and invoices section. Payment method, billing address, tax IDs and the full invoice history are all there. Invoices are also reachable from the Invoices row in the settings menu, which opens the same portal.

articles.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), seat governance & team permissions
articles.summary: Assign granular user roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Evaluator) and govern workspace permissions.
articles.html:
RBAC permission matrix

Role Tender Drafting Evidence Vault Team Management Billing & Security
Owner Full access Full access Full access Full access
Admin Full access Full access Invite & manage View only
Member Create & edit Upload & cite No access No access
Evaluator (Public Sector) Read-only Review only No access No access

Inviting team members

  1. Go to Settings > Team.
  2. Click Invite member.
  3. Enter email and assign the appropriate RBAC role.
  4. Invitations expire automatically after 7 days if unaccepted.

articles.title: Security baselines, MFA enforcement, recovery codes & data controls
articles.summary: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA/Passkeys), session policies, and corporate data protection.
articles.html:
Security controls

Velstrian Tenderworks enforces enterprise security controls to protect tender intellectual property and sensitive commercial proposals.

Recommended security configurations

  • MFA / Passkeys: Enforce TOTP or FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware passkeys for all organisation users.
  • Session Inactivity Timeout: Configure automatic sign-out after 15 to 60 minutes of inactivity.
  • IP Restriction: Restrict workspace logins to corporate VPN and office IP ranges.

articles.title: Immutable compliance audit trails, session logs & export forensics
articles.summary: Track user actions, data modifications, export timestamps and security events for internal and external audits.
articles.html:
Audit trail overview

Velstrian Tenderworks maintains an immutable log of organisation activities to support compliance, ISO 27001 certifications, and procurement audit requirements.

What gets recorded

  • Authentication: Logins, MFA verifications, password resets and session terminations.
  • User management: Member invitations, role changes, and removals.
  • Bid activities: Tender workspace creation, requirement modifications, and answer approvals.
  • Evidence vault: Document uploads, version updates, metadata edits, and deletions.
  • Data exports: Who requested an export, export format, and timestamp.

Viewing and exporting logs

  1. Navigate to Settings > Audit Log (available to Owners and Admins).
  2. Filter by date range, user, action category or severity level.
  3. Select Export CSV to generate a verifiable record for compliance teams.

articles.title: Support SLA, escalation matrix, diagnostic bug reporting & booked sessions
articles.summary: Understand support response times, diagnostic in-app issue reporting, and priority escalation paths.
articles.html:
Support channels & SLAs

Channel Availability Target Response SLA Best used for
AI Assistant (CrowChat) 24/7/365 Instantaneous (<2s) Workflow navigation, guideline search, TOMs explanations.
In-App Bug Reporter 24/7 <4 hours (business hours) Reporting technical defects with diagnostic session data.
Priority Email Support Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00 GMT <2 hours (Pro & Portfolio) Billing inquiries, SAML configuration, procurement advice.
30-Min Strategy Call By appointment Scheduled via Calendly Onboarding review, tender setup, team training.

How to file an effective diagnostic report

When reporting an issue from Help and support, the system automatically packages your browser version, viewport, URL, and anonymised request ID so our engineering team can isolate the issue immediately without back-and-forth debugging.
